name: sauce andalouse
instructions:
The belgian red-pepper mayonnaise: pureed red bell pepper + tomato paste + white wine vinegar + mayonnaise + cayenne. From Spring Council / Southern Roots.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- canned red bell peppers (in olive oil — see notes)
- tomato paste
- white wine vinegar (the best pick — see the vinegar ranking)
- mayonnaise
- cayenne pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PUREE the canned red bell pepper in a BLENDER.
2. Mix the rest in with a spoon — though sometimes the MAYO CLUMPS; if it does, a quick blitz brings it together.
notes:
=== SOURCE ===

Spring Council / Southern Roots.

=== CANNED PEPPERS IN OLIVE OIL ===

Get the canned red bell peppers packed IN OLIVE OIL — same logic as [[romesco]]: they come fire-roasted, cheap, pre-salted, and with their own flavor-infused oil.

=== THE VINEGAR RANKING — ALL THREE WORK; WHITE WINE WINS ===

All the white vinegar types were tested — white wine, champagne, and white balsamic — and ALL WORK here (unlike the cream vinaigrette, where champagne is inedible). The ranking: WHITE WINE VINEGAR best, then WHITE BALSAMIC, then CHAMPAGNE. The mayo base is apparently more forgiving of the whole family than cream is — but the sharp-clean pick leads.

=== THE MAYO CLUMPS ===

You can mix everything after the pepper puree in with a spoon, but sometimes the mayo clumps — blitz briefly if so.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[romesco]]: the other canned-red-pepper sauce — nuts and no mayo there.
- [[relish]] / [[persillade]]: the condiment shelf.
- [[chicken-tenders]]: the obvious dipping target.
